thesis: Convert Kahane-style ultraflat {0,1}-coefficient polynomials Q with ~n/2 ones into a Littlewood polynomial P = Q − Q^c (±1 coefficients, same degree) and prove a pointwise bound |Q·conj(Q^c)| ≤ (c+o(1))n/2 on a subsequence, yielding sup|P| ≤ (1+O(c))√n and hence the NEGATIVE close.

Derive the literal negation of the canonical statement from ultraflat Littlewood polynomial existence via a degree-coverage patching lemma (Kahane base + unboundedness-only coverage), which needs no density-one or full-uniformity strengthening.

statement: Exact enumeration n≤3 (heuristic n≤16) shows min M/√n > 1.5, but the asymptotic "all large n" claim admits no finite-reduction certificate; the c>0 uniform lower bound remains open, so this is evidence only, never a close of branch A or B.
No analytic reduction and no explicit finite residual claim supplied; certifier fails closed, nothing to verify exactly or by outward intervals.
Rudin–Shapiro gives |P| ≤ √(2(n+1)) for dyadic n (all n via Kahane); true, but it is a dual upper bound that neither closes branch A nor B.
Parseval gives sup ≥ √(n+1) exactly, but constant 1/2·√n-level; nowhere near (1+c)√n, so it cannot anchor branch A or B without a new mechanism.

L1's hypothesis is an open ultraflat problem in its own right and its conclusion is equivalent in strength to the canonical claim (equivalent-strength reduction, K4-type trap); no proof exists either direction, so it can be neither PROVED nor FALSE on current evidence.
